problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series if the $4$th term is $250$ and the common ratio is $5?$

activity_context.topic_title: The Sum of the First N Terms of a Geometric Series

feedback.problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series if the $5$th term is $2\,500$ and the common ratio is $5?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We use the formula for the $n$th term of a geometric sequence to determine ${a}_{1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}{r}^{n-1} \\ 2\,500 & ={a}_{1}\cdot {5}^{(5-1)} \\ 2\,500 & ={a}_{1}\cdot {5}^{4} \\ 2\,500 & =625{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =4\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case, ${a}_{1}=4$ and $r=5.$ Substituting our values into the formula for ${S}_{N}$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{4(1-{5}^{N})}{1-5} \\  & =\frac{4}{(-4)}(1-{5}^{N}) \\  & =-(1-{5}^{N}) \\  & ={5}^{N}-1\end{aligned}
$$
